alternatives.option: Exempt evidence_class legacy_unverified from the ancestor-membership requirement
alternatives.reason_rejected: the import ingress admits every class, so a hostile peer could publish legacy_unverified events with parents:[] and have them admitted without any grant — a real widening of R03/R17

alternatives.option: Make replicaKnowsAPolicy() ordering-relative (only count memberships whose event id sorts before the event's)
alternatives.reason_rejected: ULIDs are author-minted, so forging a low id becomes a cheaper bypass than the parents:[] one the existing guard was written to stop

alternatives.option: Persist the originating ingress in the journal and exempt ingress 'migration'
alternatives.reason_rejected: needs a schema column and rebuild currently hard-codes ingress 'import' when re-journaling, so it is a larger change than the merge warrants; recorded as a separate finding

context: Merged lane/02c-migration into foundation/v3; resolved the commands.ts and registry-count conflicts keeping both lanes' commands, and fixed a cross-lane admission non-monotonicity that wiped every projection on rebuild.
rationale: Lane 02b's ancestor-membership capability check (D29) falls back to a REPLICA-state question ('do I hold a policy?') when the event has no membership ancestor. That makes the verdict non-monotonic in time: lane 02c's migrated legacy corpus was admitted under the policy-free bootstrap regime, then the scenario created a membership, and on rebuild all 45 legacy events flipped to quarantined no_policy_yet / pending_parents — projections went from 45 records to 5 and the projection digest stopped reproducing, violating ADR §12 step 6 and D29's own 'at first admission AND on rebuild'. The admission_log is first-party local evidence (written by logAdmission on this machine, replayed from the durable receipt log before admit() runs), so honouring it cannot be forged by a peer the way author-controlled parents/ULIDs can. It only ever preserves a verdict this replica already reached; it never admits an event seen for the first time and does not touch the terminal 'lacks capability' answer. It is the same rule as C14 N1/N2/N3 — never silently revoke what was already admitted.
summary: Made admission monotonic for events this replica already admitted: when the bootstrap branch would quarantine no_policy_yet, honour a prior 'admitted' outcome for the same (event id, digest) in this replica's own admission_log
